title: PIRP note from F1: every section written + planted facts recalled
hypothesis: The PIRP template produces a complete note that captures the session's key facts.

sections.title: Problem
sections.html: Client presented for a 50-minute individual CBT session focusing on Panic Disorder (F41.0). Client reported a rough week, including a panic attack at a grocery store checkout on Tuesday characterized by a pounding heart and thoughts of passing out in front of others. Client completed two of three assigned thought records. Client reported poor sleep, averaging about four hours per night and waking around 3:00 AM. Client noted starting a new medication, sertraline 50 mg, prescribed by their primary care doctor two weeks ago, with initial nausea that has since resolved. Client denied any thoughts of self-harm or suicidal ideation. Client also expressed frustration regarding unhelpful support from a family member.

sections.title: Intervention
sections.html:
• Reviewed completed thought records and examined the cognitive shift in belief ratings from the peak of anxiety to post-event reflection.
  • Conducted psychoeducation regarding the physiological course of panic and safety behaviors.
  • Administered in-session interoceptive exposure by having the Client spin in a chair for 30 seconds to induce dizziness intentionally, followed by tracking anxiety ratings and recovery time.
  • Discussed potential family involvement to psychoeducate the Client's sister, which the Client deferred for a later time.
  • Utilized cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT) modalities.

sections.title: Response
sections.html: Client engaged collaboratively with the session interventions despite reporting initial apprehension. During the interoceptive spinning exercise, the Client's anxiety peaked at a rating of six and decreased to a three within two minutes, recognizing experientially that physical sensations peak and pass without fleeing the situation. Client successfully identified the cognitive drop in belief regarding passing out from 90% in the moment to 40% at home when reviewing thought records.

sections.title: Plan
sections.html:
• Complete thought records three times prior to the next session.
  • Practice the interoceptive spinning exercise once daily at home.
  • Conduct a behavioral experiment on Saturday morning by returning to the grocery store during a quiet time and remaining until anxiety decreases by half.
  • Attend individual CBT session at the same time next week.
